title: Marguerite and the Colony
premise: Zephyrine Iversen tends the Verdance, a terraformed garden on the fringe moon Calloway's Rest, and maintains a beacon broadcasting a false signal of an armed colony that doesn't exist — a lie that has kept two rival fleets from claiming the system for thirty years. When gravity flickers for nine seconds, both fleets dispatch ships to investigate, and Zephyrine must sustain the deception while falling for Wren Okafor, the defector pilot sent by one fleet to scout the 'colony.' As the lie unravels, Zephyrine discovers the beacon was commissioned by their own grandmother, who built the garden as an inheritance for refugees rather than soldiers. In the end, Zephyrine broadcasts the truth — the garden itself, alive and thriving — and both fleets, moved by what the Verdance represents, agree to share stewardship; Zephyrine and Wren choose each other over duty, becoming the colony's first true inhabitants.
about_author: Ulyana Sandoval is a former hydroponics engineer who spent six years on orbital agriculture projects before turning to fiction full-time. She writes quiet, plant-forward science fiction about people who maintain things nobody thanks them for.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. While pruning in the Verdance, gravity fails for exactly nine seconds; soil, water, and Zephyrine hang suspended as the beacon hums beneath them. When gravity returns, every instrument reads normal — except the beacon logged the anomaly too. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine, the sense that something vast just noticed them.

chapters.title: The Garden for Nobody
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with flashbacks to arriving on Calloway's Rest five years ago. We learn the Verdance was commissioned for colonists who never came, and the beacon broadcasts a garrison signal Zephyrine merely maintains without understanding. Emotional beat: loneliness reframed as devotion; tending beauty for absent people.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Admiral Sefu Idris of the Meridian Fleet and Captain Lysa Voss of the Halcyon Compact each detect the nine-second anomaly and independently conclude the 'garrison' may be compromised. Both order scout ships. Emotional beat: cold institutional dread on both sides, the reader seeing the trap closing from two directions.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Digging into the beacon's maintenance logs to explain the flicker, Zephyrine finds encrypted files older than their tenure — commissioning documents sealed under a name they half-recognize: Iversen. Emotional beat: the first crack in Zephyrine's understanding of their own inheritance.

chapters.title: A Ship Called Patience
chapters.summary: Wren Okafor's POV. Aboard the Meridian scout ship Patience, Wren — a decorated pilot secretly disillusioned with the war economy — approaches Calloway's Rest under stealth. They observe a lush garden where intelligence promised a military base. Emotional beat: wonder colliding with suspicion; Wren decides to land alone.

chapters.title: The Visitor at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Alternating Zephyrine and Wren POVs. Wren lands and claims to be a stranded freighter pilot; Zephyrine, starved for company, almost believes it — until they spot the military-grade thruster scorch marks. Emotional beat: wary hospitality, two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: Tomatoes and Interrogation
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Over three days of shared meals, Wren probes for evidence of a garrison and finds only greenhouses, seed vaults, and one exhausted gardener. Zephyrine deflects with practiced ease but begins enjoying the company. Emotional beat: intimacy growing inside mutual deception; guilt taking root.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Vault
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Using Wren's arrival as pretext to open the sealed sublevel, Zephyrine decrypts the commissioning file: Odile Iversen, Zephyrine's grandmother, built the beacon and the garden together — the fake garrison designed to keep fleets out so the Verdance could mature into a refuge. Emotional beat: awe and betrayal; family love revealed as strategic fiction.

chapters.title: Signal Traffic
chapters.summary: Admiral Idris's POV. The Patience goes silent past its check-in window; Idris, pressured by hawks who want the system seized regardless, orders a battle group to follow the scout's trajectory. Emotional beat: a decent man feeling his options narrow; duty hardening into momentum.

chapters.title: Confession in the Orchid House
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Wren admits being Meridian's scout; Zephyrine admits there is no garrison, no colony — only the lie. Instead of reporting back, Wren asks to see everything. Emotional beat: relief and terror entwined; the truth spoken aloud for the first time in thirty years.

chapters.title: Captain Voss Moves First
chapters.summary: Lysa Voss's POV. The Compact, having tracked the same anomaly, jumps a fast frigate into the system ahead of Meridian's battle group, intending to seize the beacon and expose or exploit the garrison. Emotional beat: ruthless competence; Voss sees the garden not as a refuge but as leverage.

chapters.title: Counting Days
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. With both fleets inbound, Zephyrine and Wren calculate the impossible math: the beacon can't fake a battle-ready garrison against actual sensors at close range. They have perhaps eleven days. Emotional beat: clock-tight dread tempered by the strange peace of working side by side.

chapters.title: What Odile Left Growing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Exploring the deep archive, Wren finds Odile's personal logs: she seeded the Verdance with crops and trees engineered to feed ten thousand refugees, and wrote letters to grandchildren she might never meet. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; Wren begins to believe the garden is worth defending.

chapters.title: The Hawk's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Meridian's hawk faction delivers an ultimatum: take the system by force when the battle group arrives, or be relieved of command. Idris sends one final hail to the surface demanding proof of the garrison. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; a man looking for any reason not to fire.

chapters.title: Eleven Hours of Static
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The Compact frigate arrives first and jams the beacon, then demands surrender. Zephyrine stalls via comms while Wren secretly reconfigures the Patience's transponder to mimic garrison chatter. Emotional beat: improvisation under pressure; the lie now held up by two pairs of hands.

chapters.title: Voss Descends
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Landing with a boarding party, Voss walks the Verdance expecting a mask and finds abundance — orchards, nurseries, a seed library for peoples not yet born. Her certainty wavers even as she arrests Zephyrine. Emotional beat: ideology meeting something it cannot categorize.

chapters.title: The Battle Group Arrives
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Meridian's battle group drops into the system to find a Compact frigate on the ground and a 'garrison' transmitting defiance. Weapons arm on both sides. On the surface, Wren hijacks the beacon to broadcast Odile's logs system-wide. Emotional beat: brinkmanship; the whole story converging on nine seconds again.

chapters.title: Gravity Fails Again
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The beacon's overloaded systems trigger a second nine-second null-gravity event — this time felt by every ship in orbit. In the shared weightlessness, weapons lock, both fleets hear Odile's voice reading her letters. Emotional beat: suspended stillness as enemies float together inside someone else's dream.

chapters.title: The Choice of Captains
chapters.summary: Idris and Voss dual POV. Confronted with the truth — no garrison, no colony, only a garden built as inheritance — each captain must defy their own chain of command. Idris refuses the hawk order to fire; Voss orders her frigate to stand down and offers parley on the surface. Emotional beat: courage redefined as refusal.

chapters.title: Parley Among the Fruit Trees
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Under the oldest apple trees, Idris, Voss, Wren, and freed Zephyrine negotiate: the Verdance becomes neutral ground, its seed vault open to both fleets' refugee populations, stewarded jointly. Emotional beat: exhaustion giving way to fragile, negotiated hope.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Weeks later, the first settlers from both fleets arrive — not soldiers but families, engineers, the displaced. Zephyrine and Wren, having chosen the garden over their respective services, plant a new row together and finally read Odile's last letter aloud. Emotional beat: belonging achieved; love and duty reconciled at last.

chapters.title: The Beacon Keeps Its Promise
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Zephyrine's POV. One year on, Zephyrine reprograms the beacon to broadcast not a lie but an invitation — coordinates, harvest reports, a welcome. Standing in the Verdance at dusk with Wren, they watch new lights descend through the atmosphere. Emotional beat: quiet fulfillment; the garden finally holding the people it was grown for.
